decision_text: Stage G is complete at evaluations 2 and 3 of 4. g1-ih-half (Ih halved) is rejected on its registered clause: the 250 pA count stays 8; it moved the rest -1.7 mV and the 310 pA rate -0.23 Hz, kept axon-first initiation and every width verdict, and moved the sweep-43 late return -0.7 mV (allowed), so halving Ih translates the resting potential without rotating the f-I curve. g2-leak-150 (leak x1.5) is rejected on the sweep-43 return (moved -3.1..-3.8 mV, past the donor) and on the 310 pA count (6 < 8, rate 6.02 Hz); its registered pure-shift clause is not met because the drops differ (-8 at 250 pA, -4 at 310 pA), i.e. the leak rotates the curve, but by collapsing 250 pA to silence (plateau -66.8 mV) rather than landing it near 5. The registered dose rule names g2 as the better arm (g1's ratio is 0) and a linear dose of leak_factor 1.1875, whose interpolated 310 rate change (-1.51 Hz) and sweep-43 move (-1.15 mV) both sit outside their constraints, so no admissible dose exists under the rule. The G3 selection recorded here is therefore the coordinator's registered Dissection-rule alternative (combined Ih half + leak x1.5 on B3); it is not run, and the additive reading of the two arms predicts it fails every Stage G band. Under the manifest fail_rule the campaign stands at FAIL with 3 of 4 evaluations spent unless the coordinator elects to spend evaluation 4 on the combined arm.
